page: Microsoft Azure E64_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The server is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. Multi-core performance is highlighted by a strong stress-ng multi-core score of 62127.65 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 16157.0. Large-block memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 286.33 GB/sec for read operations and 130.34 GB/sec for write operations. Single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1638.0. The system excels in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operations, though it shows weak performance in large-scale LLM text generation, such as 2.74 tokens/sec on a 70B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64_v5 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications, reducing the need to scale out to larger clusters. However, the absence of local storage requires users to provision external storage, which may impact overall infrastructure costs and I/O latency. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational databases, large-scale data compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
